title: Normalized scalar adjunction on K-flat models and the coefficient unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a final object [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $n\geq1$, and put $Z=\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ and $R=(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal C}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their cohomological unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $E=-\otimes_Z R$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $Lq=-\otimes_Z^L R$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and let $\operatorname{Res}$ be restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Restriction is exact, and its right derived functor is termwise restriction. The ordinary adjunction $E\dashv\operatorname{Res}$ is specified by the inverse formulas $f\mapsto(a\mapsto f(a\otimes\bar1))$ and $g\mapsto(a\otimes r\mapsto r g(a))$. Let the derived adjunction be the one supplied by [new-derived-adjunction-compatibility] on K-flat resolving complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Writing $\eta$ for its unit, for every K-flat complex $P$ the resolution comparison $c_P:Lq(P)\simeq E(P)$ satisfies
$$(\operatorname{Res}c_P)\eta_P=Q(P\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}E(P)),\qquad x\longmapsto x\otimes\bar1,$$
where $Q$ denotes localization of complexes. With the shift structure on $Lq$ induced by this adjunction and exact restriction, $\eta$ commutes with every integer shift: $\eta_{X[k]}=\eta_X[k]$, with the canonical shift comparisons inserted.
The integer unit complex $Z[0]$ is K-flat, and there is a unique isomorphism $e:Lq(Z[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}R[0]$ whose adjunct is the actual coefficient quotient $q:Z[0]\to\operatorname{Res}R[0]$, that is
$$(\operatorname{Res}e)\eta_Z=q.$$
For any abelian sheaf $F$, residue-module sheaf $T$, quotient map $p:F\to\operatorname{Res}T$ with $p$ a cokernel of $n:F\to F$, and isomorphism $a:Lq(F[0])\simeq T[0]$ normalized by $(\operatorname{Res}a)\eta_F=p[0]$, every sheaf map $s:Z\to F$ has a unique residue-linear reduction $\bar s:R\to T$ satisfying $(\operatorname{Res}\bar s)q=ps$. Its map in the derived category satisfies
$$\bar s[0]=a\,Lq(s[0])\,e^{-1}.$$
All comparisons here use the natural single-complex/restriction identifications; no flatness of $R$ over $Z$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the ordinary coefficient adjunction to the ring-sheaf map $Z\to R$. Its restriction functor preserves finite limits and finite colimits, hence is exact. In the ordering $E(A)=A\otimes_ZR$, its Hom map sends $f$ to $g(x)=f(x\otimes\bar1)$. The inverse sends $g$ to $x\otimes r\mapsto r g(x)$: this is balanced, additive and $R$-linear, and hence extends uniquely over the sheafified tensor. The two composites are identities since $\bar1 g(x)=g(x)$ and $f(x\otimes r)=r f(x\otimes\bar1)$. All formulas mean maps after the sheafification unit; no assertion that every tensor section is a global pure tensor is used. Thus the ordinary unit $u_A$ is $x\mapsto x\otimes\bar1$.

source.place: Tags 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules) and 03DA (lemma-abelian); lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict, inverse maps on pure tensors.

proof.text:
Because restriction is exact, its termwise derived factorization computes its right derived functor on every complex; use it as $\operatorname{Res}$, with its canonical comparison $\beta$. All transition maps of the ind-system $(Q\operatorname{Res}K')_{K\to K'}$ are then invertible, so it is essentially constant with stage $\mathrm{id}_K$. The termwise adjunction descends to the homotopy categories. The derived change-of-rings theorem supplies the comparison $c_M:Lq(QM)\to Q(EM)$, invertible for K-flat $M$; $Lq$ is everywhere defined and computed by K-flat resolutions, which exist for every complex. So the pro-systems $(QE(P))_{P\to M}$ are essentially constant with value $Lq(M)$, a K-flat resolution being the stage. These are the hypotheses of derived-adjunction compatibility. It fixes the adjunction $Lq\dashv\operatorname{Res}$ of the statement. Its canonical Hom formula is the pre-derived formula at identity denominators:
$$\Phi_{QM,QN}\bigl(Q(f)c_M\bigr)=\beta_N Q(g)$$
for every complex map $f:EM\to N$ with ordinary transpose $g:M\to\operatorname{Res}N$, where $\Phi(h)=\operatorname{Res}(h)\eta$. The general-site derived Hom comparison gives an adjunction with this same formula. The two agree: with $M$ K-flat and $f=1_{EM}$, the formula gives $\operatorname{Res}(c_M)\eta_{QM}=\beta Q(u_M)$, and $c_M$ is invertible. Thus both units agree on every K-flat $QM$. Every object is isomorphic to such a $QM$, and units are natural, so the units agree everywhere, hence so do the Hom bijections. Below, $\beta$ is suppressed. No flat terms in $M$ and no flatness of $R$ are used.

proof.text:
In the preceding formula put $M=P$, $N=E P$ and $f=1_{E P}$. Its ordinary transpose is $u_P$ term by term. Therefore
$$\operatorname{Res}(c_P)\eta_{QP}=\Phi(c_P)=Q(u_P).$$
For K-flat $P$ the comparison $c_P$ is an isomorphism, so this is exactly the claimed normalization, with $u_P(x)=x\otimes\bar1$.

source.place: Tags 0FND and 09T5: the comparison formula specialized to the identity on E(P).

proof.text:
Termwise exact restriction commutes with every integer shift: it preserves the differential $(-1)^k d$ by additivity, and the reassociation and zero-shift comparisons are termwise identities. Transfer this shift structure across $Lq\dashv\operatorname{Res}$ using the dual of clause (iii) of the adjunction shift-compatibility lemma. Explicitly apply that clause to the opposite adjunction $\operatorname{Res}^{\mathrm{op}}\dashv Lq^{\mathrm{op}}$, with opposite shifts defined by $[k]_{\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}}=([-k]_{\mathcal D})^{\mathrm{op}}$. It gives the compatible structure on $Lq^{\mathrm{op}}$; returning to the original categories gives the required structure on $Lq$. The lemma's simultaneous unit and counit compatibility transfers back as well (opposition interchanges unit and counit). If $\lambda_{X,k}:Lq(X[k])\simeq Lq(X)[k]$ and $\rho_{Y,k}:\operatorname{Res}(Y[k])\simeq\operatorname{Res}(Y)[k]$, its unit equation is
$$\rho_{LqX,k}\operatorname{Res}(\lambda_{X,k})\eta_{X[k]}=\eta_X[k].$$
This is the asserted shift equation for the shift structure induced by this adjunction.

proof.text: The sheaf tensor universal property gives $A\otimes_Z Z\simeq A$ by $x\otimes z\mapsto zx$, with inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. These maps are inverse on the generating pure tensors, hence inverse on sheaves. Consequently for every complex $A^\bullet$, the degree-$j$ term of $\operatorname{Tot}(A^\bullet\otimes_Z Z[0])$ is $A^j\otimes_Z Z\simeq A^j$, and its differential is $d_A^j$ under this identification: the second tensor factor has zero differential and degree zero. For acyclic $A^\bullet$ the tensor total complex is thus acyclic. This is precisely the definition that $Z[0]$ is K-flat.

source.place: Tag 06YN (definition-K-flat); tensor unit verified directly from sites-modules.tex Section 03EK universal property.

proof.text:
Define $b:E(Z[0])\simeq R[0]$ by $z\otimes r\mapsto q(z)r$, with inverse $r\mapsto1\otimes r$. The balanced tensor relations show that both composites are identities; the tensor universal property makes these inverse sheaf maps. Put $e=Q(b)c_{Z[0]}$. The preceding K-flat calculation and the derived comparison make $e$ an isomorphism. The unit formula of Step 3 gives
$$\operatorname{Res}(e)\eta_Z=Q(\operatorname{Res}(b)u_Z)=q,$$
because $\operatorname{Res}(b)u_Z$ sends $z$ to $q(z)\bar1=q(z)$. Thus the comparison is normalized by the actual coefficient quotient, rather than an unspecified automorphism of $R[0]$.

source.place: Tag 06YU and the change-of-rings construction before it; sites-modules.tex Section 03EK, tensor unit maps.

proof.text: If $e'$ has the same prescribed adjunct $q$, then $\Phi(e')=q=\Phi(e)$. Injectivity of the Hom bijection gives $e'=e$, even among all morphisms $Lq(Z[0])\to R[0]$. This proves the required uniqueness among isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 0FND and 09T5, injectivity of the derived Hom correspondence.

proof.text:
For $s:Z\to F$, let $v:E(Z)\to T$ be the ordinary adjunct of $ps:Z\to\operatorname{Res}T$. With the degree-zero tensor unit $b_0:E(Z)\simeq R$ of Step 6, define $\bar s=v b_0^{-1}$. Then
$$(\operatorname{Res}\bar s)q=(\operatorname{Res}v)(\operatorname{Res}b_0^{-1})q=(\operatorname{Res}v)u_Z=ps.$$
Conversely any $R$-linear $t:R\to T$ satisfying this equation makes $t b_0$ an ordinary adjunct of $ps$, hence $t b_0=v$ and $t=\bar s$. This proves existence and uniqueness without identifying a sheaf cokernel with a sectionwise cokernel. The stated cokernel hypothesis on $p$ is retained; this reduction argument only needs that $T$ is an $R$-module and $p$ is an abelian sheaf map.

source.place: Tag 03D7 and lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict, applied at the source Z and target T.

proof.text:
Use naturality of the derived unit and the normalization assumed for $a$ to compute
$$\Phi\bigl(a Lq(s[0])\bigr)=\operatorname{Res}(a)\operatorname{Res}(Lq(s[0]))\eta_Z=\operatorname{Res}(a)\eta_F s[0]=p[0]s[0].$$
On the other hand, the normalizations of $e$ and $\bar s$ give
$$\Phi\bigl(\bar s[0]e\bigr)=(\operatorname{Res}\bar s[0])\operatorname{Res}(e)\eta_Z=(\operatorname{Res}\bar s[0])q=p[0]s[0].$$
Injectivity of $\Phi$ yields $\bar s[0]e=a Lq(s[0])$. Postcompose on the source with $e^{-1}$ to obtain $\bar s[0]=a Lq(s[0])e^{-1}$. Termwise restriction of a degree-zero complex is the degree-zero complex of the restricted sheaf, so these are exactly the single-complex comparisons in the statement.
